result:
I've reviewed the full diff, both prior gate reviews, the evidence, and the surrounding source (edge/prov construction, `build_project_graph` gating, the `GraphEdge`/`ProjectGraph` dataclasses, and the preserved regex JS pass). Here is my Gate C verdict.

```json
{
  "verdict": "ACCEPT_WITH_CHANGES",
  "mustFixBeforeMerge": [
    "Same-file Python calls/inherits over-claim 'deterministic' via trailing-name matching. `_ast_reference_name` returns the trailing attr for `ast.Attribute`, so `<any_receiver>.helper()` resolves to a unique same-file module function `helper` (confidence=deterministic), and `class C(some.mod.Base)` resolves to a same-file class `Base`. The receiver is ignored, so common method names (get/post/run/close/start) colliding with module-level function names mint false deterministic 'calls' edges. Endpoints are real nodes (not fabricated), but the label is wrong and the confidence is overstated. Fix: for the same-file DETERMINISTIC Python path, require an `ast.Name` callee/base, or downgrade attribute-qualified same-file matches to 'heuristic'. Add a negative test (e.g. `obj.helper()` with a same-file `def helper` -> no deterministic edge). NOTE: Gate B explicitly blessed the same-file attribute-call behavior, so confirm this is intentional rather than silently shipping it."
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Cross-file Python resolution is well-guarded and anti-fabrication-safe: param/local bound-name stack, same-file skip, exact (alias.asname or alias.name) binding map, single-candidate (len==1) requirement, `caller.path != target.path` to avoid duplicating P1. Negative tests cover shadowed locals, unknown receivers, and name-only calls. JS calls only resolve bare `identifier` callees via import bindings or unique same-file label — no repo-wide name guessing.",
    "Determinism is sound: `_ts_sorted_descendants` sorts by (start_byte,end_byte,type); import-binding walk sorted by (lineno,col_offset,typename); function scopes sorted by (start_byte,id); alias/target sets only consumed under len==1; final sort-by-id retained. `_edge` folds confidence|derived_by into the id hash for calls/inherits so deterministic and heuristic edges to different targets cannot collide. Determinism tests build twice and assert canonical-JSON + node/edge id-order equality.",
    "Contract safety holds: the regex JS pass still runs; tree-sitter dedups module/import/top-level-function nodes by id (identical `module.name` symbols) via `_add_node_with_defined_edge`/`setdefault`, and only ADDS classes, methods, and arrow functions. GraphEdge.confidence/derived_by pre-existed with these exact defaults, so existing non-calls/inherits edges remain byte-identical. Protected/generated/excluded files are skipped in both new passes (and `_add_python_nodes` is already gated identically).",
    "Test adequacy is strong for the new branches (each import form, resolved/unresolved, multi-candidate drop, shadowing, dedup, JS+TS, determinism) and the fail_under=100 gate is enforced — but it lacks the negative case for the attribute-base/attribute-call same-file trailing-name path called out above."
  ],
  "residualRisks": [
    "`metadata={'tree_sitter': _tree_sitter_metadata()}` embeds live importlib-reported parser versions into `canonical_graph_json`. Every graph — including pure-Python repos that now always carry this block — changes canonical output whenever a tree-sitter dep is bumped, silently invalidating any stored golden/snapshot hash. Exact `==` pins + uv.lock keep it reproducible today; revisit goldens on any parser bump. The `_package_version` 'unknown' branch is effectively dead since the three packages are hard top-level imports.",
    "schema_version stays 'project-graph/v0.1' despite a new top-level `metadata` field, new edge kinds (calls/inherits), and the first-ever 'heuristic' confidence emission. Downstream consumers keyed on schema_version won't detect the shape change (raised by Gate A and B; a version-note/bump decision is still open).",
    "project_model_gate.HIGH_IMPACT_EDGE_KINDS includes 'calls' and flags supporting edges with confidence != 'deterministic'. These heuristic python_ast/treesitter calls are the first non-deterministic high-impact edges; if any contract auto-selects one as a supporting edge it will newly trip contract_references. Calibration gate passed per evidence, but confirm no consumer auto-selects heuristic calls as contract support.",
    "JS heritage resolution uses `_javascript_first_identifier` (leading identifier of class_heritage), so `extends ns.Base` or call-expression heritage resolve on the leading token and are dropped unless a class of that name exists — low risk of misresolution rather than fabrication. JS member-expression calls (`a.b()`) are skipped entirely (conservative; no method-call edges)."
  ]
}
```
